spec.title: Advisory central custody and explicit same-machine handoff

p.CUSTODY-SCOPE: Custody coordinates owner-facing central sessions that share one user-local context on one machine. Its ordinary `vacant`/`held` state, epoch, holder, session and heartbeat fields are diagnostic observations. They do not gate central plan mutation, worker acceptance, commits, pushes or campaign-status promotion.

p.CUSTODY-NOT-PERMISSION: Custody is neither repository permission nor a security lock. Owner instruction and project authority govern every operation. A valid `offering` created by an explicit owner-requested formal handoff is the sole protocol write fence.

p.CASUAL-CONTINUATION: A timeout, crash, compaction, new chat or model change is ordinary continuation. Any owner-facing central agent may resolve the exact binding, read settings and the complete plan, verify the repository tree and continue under the current owner instruction without creating session, handoff, receipt or takeover records. Stale, vacant or mismatched custody metadata does not require a claim or takeover.

p.CONTINUATION-DESIGN-DECISION: **Decision:** ordinary continuation is ritual-free; the two-phase custody protocol is opt-in only after explicit owner handoff intent. **Why:** session timeout and restart are routine, while manufacturing transfer documents and rereading their copied context adds substantial latency and token cost without adding authority. **Considered and rejected:** mandatory takeover on every session identity change recreates the reported failure; deleting formal handoff entirely loses a useful owner-requested audit trail. **When to revisit:** an observed concurrent-write incident escapes the coherent-input checks, or the owner requests a stricter default coordination mode.

p.CONCURRENT-WRITER-SAFETY: Before mutation, compare the observed plan and repository inputs with the current bytes/tree. An empirically observed live conflicting central writer or input drift stops writes, preserves artifacts and asks the owner to select the writer. Freshness metadata is an alarm to investigate, while staleness alone is not proof of absence, presence or authority. Never settle a conflict by newest timestamp.

format.title: 2. `custody.toml` reference format
format.fence: schema = 1 context_id = "3d7a79bf-5f27-4b88-9eaa-c8323df5cb03" epoch = 7 state = "held" holder_id = "central-a-20260829" session_id = "d218b184-8d63-46d0-aed8-62dd47e6bd27" harness = "codex-desktop" planning_profile = "ultra" acquired_at = "2026-08-29T11:00:00Z" heartbeat_at = "2026-08-29T11:40:00Z" offer_id = ""

p.CUSTODY-STATES: State is `vacant | held | offering`. `vacant` and `held` are advisory. Epoch is a monotonic diagnostic observation and holder/session/harness/profile/timestamps do not grant or deny authority. `offer_id` is only a locator and must agree with a valid open formal offer. `offering` fences writes only when that offer arose from an explicit owner request. A timestamp may reveal possible liveness but never requires or self-authorizes takeover.

p.ATOMIC-CUSTODY-WRITE: When custody is updated for diagnostics or formal handoff, replace it atomically through a same-directory temporary file and rename. A partially written or missing advisory file is reported and reconstructed from binding, plan and repository evidence; it does not itself stop ordinary continuation. An active explicit formal offer remains fenced until its exact protocol repairs or terminates it.

facts.HANDOFF-PLANNED: **Planned transfer:** a live central coordinator transfers to another coordinator after the owner explicitly requests formal handoff.
facts.HANDOFF-ROLLOVER: Retired v0.2 handoff kind. Session rollover is ordinary continuation under `NOT-HANDOFF-KINDS`.
facts.HANDOFF-RECOVERY: Retired v0.2 handoff kind. Ordinary crash recovery follows `RECOVERY-CASUAL`; only repair of an already-open explicit offer remains formal.

p.NOT-HANDOFF-KINDS: Session rollover, timeout, crash, compaction, new chat and model change are not handoff kinds. They use ordinary continuation. Repair or cancellation of an already-open explicit formal offer follows §§8–9 only because formal handoff was previously requested.

p.FORMAL-INTENT-REQUIRED: Invoke this offer/receipt grammar only from explicit owner intent to prepare, accept, cancel, inspect or recover a formal handoff. Never infer it from restart, compaction, model identity, stale custody or a new chat.

p.GRAMMAR: Canonical incoming forms are `ACCEPT HANDOFF FROM <context-id>`, `RECEIVE HANDOFF FROM <context-id>`, and Russian `ПРИМИ ХЭНДОФФ ИЗ <context-id>`. Recognise intent rather than casing or exact inflection. `context-id` is the opaque UUID directory name; never parse user, repository, branch or model from it.

p.OPEN-OFFER-RESOLUTION: Scan only that context's `handoffs/*/offer.toml` and terminal sibling records. A context-only phrase succeeds when exactly one valid `status = "offered"` bundle has neither `receipt.toml` nor `cancellation.toml`. Zero open offers refuses `HANDOFF_NOT_FOUND`; more than one refuses `HANDOFF_AMBIGUOUS` and lists ids without reading a winner. The explicit form `ACCEPT HANDOFF <handoff-id> FROM <context-id>` selects one. Timestamp, directory order and “latest” never decide custody.

p.NO-PASTED-BODY: The command is a locator, not a carrier. The incoming session reads the stored offer, complete `HANDOFF.md`, plan and attachments from disk. The owner does not paste or restate their contents in chat.

p.BUNDLE-HOME: One bundle lives at `handoffs/<UTC>-<opaque-handoff-id>/`. The outgoing coordinator creates `offer.toml` and `HANDOFF.md`; the incoming coordinator alone creates `receipt.toml`. Sealed files are immutable. Corrections create a new offer that supersedes the old id.

p.HANDOFF-FILE-IS-A-DELIVERABLE: Creation is not complete until the outgoing procedure has materialised the comprehensive `HANDOFF.md` itself. A chat summary, pointer to chat history, or instruction for the owner to paste context is not a deliverable.

p.HANDOFF-BODY: `HANDOFF.md` contains at minimum: TL;DR; context and transfer reason; complete owner mandate and later rulings; architecture/policy decisions in force; full hierarchical route and expanded frontier; accepted boundary with evidence; every candidate/unaccepted artifact and exact acceptance recipe; branch, HEAD, ahead/behind and dirty-tree inventory; blockers/risks; relevant reports, cache, branches and worktrees; literal next-step recipe; current settings; cleanup prohibitions; and pointers to repository authorities. It contains no secret values.

p.BUNDLE-HASHES: `offer.toml` names source and intended receiver, context id, source epoch, proposed epoch, Git observations, plan revision, creation time, SHA-256 of `HANDOFF.md` and `plan.toml`, the current `GOAL.md`/Claude-condition hashes when available, and `acceptance_transfers = false`. Paths into the repository are repository-relative; local-only evidence may use absolute paths inside the local bundle.

offer.title: 6. Explicit outgoing procedure

facts.OFFER-VERIFY: Require the owner's explicit formal-handoff request, then verify current context, Git state, live processes and artifact locations empirically.
facts.OFFER-BACKSCAN: Backscan the entire mandate, plan, accepted evidence, candidates, worker reports, branches/worktrees and unpromoted discoveries. Repair the plan before describing it.
facts.OFFER-GOAL: Refresh deterministic `GOAL.md`/`GOAL-CLAUDE.txt` for the intended continuing campaign before hashing the bundle. If selection is ambiguous, obtain `goal_node` from the owner before offering.
facts.OFFER-WRITE: Write and hash the bundle, including a short resume pointer containing only the receive-by-context command; then set custody to `offering` with its `offer_id` and the same source epoch.
facts.OFFER-PRINT: After sealing, print the exact locator shape below with literal ids and the target-language receive phrase.

offer.fence: HANDOFF CREATED context-id: <context-id> handoff-id: <handoff-id> receive-command: ПРИМИ ХЭНДОФФ ИЗ <context-id>

p.PRINT-IS-NOT-A-WRITE: This terminal/chat output is required even though the outgoing holder is now write-fenced. It does not mutate repository or stewardship state. Do not print the full handoff body; the command is its locator.

facts.OFFER-FENCE: After the offer is sealed, the outgoing session is read-only for the repository and plan. It may answer the incoming coordinator or inspect the receipt, but any substantive repair requires owner-directed cancellation and a new epoch/offer.

facts.RECEIPT-READ: Read the project boot contract, this protocol, complete bundle and complete local plan before proposing work.
facts.RECEIPT-VERIFY: Verify hashes, context binding, repository status, HEAD/ahead/behind, dirty files and named artifact existence. Reproduce high-risk claims; do not trust the narrative where the tree can answer.
facts.RECEIPT-CLASSIFY: Classify discrepancies. Project-accepted commits/specs remain project evidence; local acceptance claims without durable evidence, dirty changes, worker reports and incomplete gates remain `candidate`.
facts.RECEIPT-WRITE: Write `receipt.toml` as `accepted | accepted-with-exceptions | rejected`, list every exception and observed mismatch, and hash the offer read.
facts.RECEIPT-CLAIM: For an accepted receipt, atomically advance custody to the proposed epoch and incoming holder. A rejected receipt leaves the offer unresolved; neither side silently writes.
facts.RECEIPT-GOAL: After an accepted formal receipt ends the `offering` fence, run `steward-goal`. Print the complete refreshed `GOAL.md` to the user, then print the exact single-line contents of `GOAL-CLAUDE.txt` in a separate fence so the human can submit the client-only `/goal` command without finding a file manually. An ambiguous goal selection is reported after custody claim and requests `goal_node`; it does not undo a valid receipt.
facts.RECEIPT-REPORT-WAIT: Report restored state, candidates, blockers and proposed next atom to the owner, then wait. Receipt completes the requested formal transfer, not permission to guess the owner's next priority.

recovery.title: 8. Ordinary recovery and interrupted formal handoff

p.RECOVERY-CASUAL: Outside a valid open explicit formal offer, recovery is ordinary continuation: resolve the binding, read settings and complete plan, inspect Git/tree and candidates, then continue under the current owner instruction. No session, handoff, receipt, takeover record or custody claim is required.

p.RECOVERY-AUTH: If an explicit formal offer is already open and a participant is unavailable, repair, cancellation or recovery of that formal transfer requires owner direction naming the context. Record the missing participant, source epoch/heartbeat, evidence of unavailability, observed Git/tree state and every unaccepted artifact. This exception does not turn ordinary restart into takeover.

p.RECOVERY-ACCEPTANCE: After repair of an interrupted explicit formal handoff, the last repository-level accepted boundary is trusted as history. Work after that boundary is candidate until independently accepted. Never infer “probably accepted” from timestamps, staged state or a worker's PASS.

p.CANCEL: A live outgoing holder may cancel an unreceipted offer only on owner direction, by writing a cancellation record and advancing epoch back to `held`. It never edits the sealed offer.

p.CANCEL-TERMINAL-RECORD: Cancellation is an immutable sibling `cancellation.toml` naming offer/context ids, source and new epochs, authorizing owner instruction, reason, instant and whether a receipt existed (false for ordinary cancellation). Offer resolution treats the bundle as terminal. An explicit attempt to receive it returns `HANDOFF_CANCELLED`, never a claim.

p.SPLIT-BRAIN: Two valid receipts claiming the same proposed epoch or repository writes from the fenced outgoing session are split-brain evidence. Stop both central writers, preserve artifacts, compare against project authority, and let the owner select a new recovery epoch. Never settle split brain by newest timestamp.
